distractors: A queue of tasks all waiting on the same person, moving only as fast as that one diary allows them to move.
Agreement reached quietly before a meeting starts, so that the discussion in the room only ratifies what was settled outside it.

A sequence of checks run automatically before a release, each one able to stop the thing going out on its own. It is machinery wired into the pipeline rather than anything a person has arranged by hand.

The order in which speakers will take an item, agreed beforehand so that nobody talks over anybody and the most senior view does not land first. It settles the choreography of the session rather than whether the material behind it holds.

A backlog cleared down before any new work is accepted, so that the team starts the next thing without carrying the last one on its back. The point is finishing what is already open, which is about closing things out rather than about being ready for a moment ahead of you.
